referenceSources.description:
A white Citroën Xsara Kit Car is parked on a narrow, winding road bordered by a stone wall. The car’s rear wing, flared wheel arches, and slick rally tires emphasize its competition‑ready setup. Prominent Michelin and Total branding on the bumper and sides highlight its sponsorship livery, while the red double‑chevron logo on the roof and “3618 W 92” license plate identify its French origins.

Developed under F2 Kit Car regulations in the late 1990s, the Xsara featured a 2.0‑liter, 280 hp engine and weighed just 960 kg. It achieved national titles in France and Spain with drivers Philippe Bugalski and Jesús “Chus” Puras, and scored notable WRC asphalt results at Rally Catalunya and Tour de Corse. The car’s advanced braking system, differential, and traction control made it a formidable asphalt specialist before FIA rule changes ended the Kit Car era.
